messages:
Maria G: Hey team — customer reports SSE stream from our hosted API drops after ~60s only when requests go through CloudFront + ALB in front of the origin. Direct to origin is stable. Any ideas?

Jen (support): Thanks Maria — any request/response headers or curl repro? Do they see partial events or a straight disconnect?

Maria G: They see completed events, then nothing, and client eventually reconnects. No error body. We asked for a tcpdump but they sent this quick repro:

curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" "https://api.example-customer.com/stream?sess=abc" | sed -n '1,120p'

and server logs show regular keepalives every 15s. With CloudFront in front we see the socket close after ~60s.

Kevin L: CloudFront is known to buffer small chunks then flush on idle or buffer thresholds. If CloudFront sees small SSE comments it may coalesce them into larger TCP frames and then drop if idle crosses its origin timeout. Do you have the CloudFront distribution set to respect origin headers (Cache-Control: no-transform)?

Tom (eng): Also check ALB idle timeout — default 60s. If ALB closes because it sees no data at TCP level (CloudFront aggregated) the client will see disconnect. Two common fixes: 1) send a consistent comment keepalive every 10s (like ": keepalive\\n\\n") so chunks are big enough; 2) set CloudFront Origin Response/Keep-Alive timeouts and disable buffering for that origin path.

Jen (support): Customer said they send ": heartbeat\\n\\n" every 15s already. Strange it still hits 60s. Could CloudFront be converting HTTP/2->HTTP/1 and merging?

Kevin L: Yep. HTTP/2 multiplexing -> HTTP/1 origin often causes chunk merging. Also some CDNs will wait for final chunk or a flush boundary. Try increasing keepalive frequency to 10s or add a slightly larger payload (e.g., ":\\u00a0\\n\\n" then a small json line) to force a non-empty chunk.

Maria G: Customer tried curl -N and observed boundaries are merged: response body looks like several events concatenated with no immediate flush. Their intermediate headers show: 

Via: 1.1 cloudfront
x-cache: Miss from cloudfront
X-Amz-Cf-Id: ABCDEF

Tom (eng): Can you paste origin response headers? We want to see Transfer-Encoding. If you use chunked on origin and set "Connection: keep-alive" + "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" CloudFront should forward but might rebuffer. Recommend to add header: "Cache-Control: no-transform" and ensure "Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8". Also include an explicit "X-Accel-Buffering: no" for nginx origins.

Maria G: Origin headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
X-Accel-Buffering: no

Kevin L: Good. Next steps: 1) escalate CloudFront support with distribution id + sample trace and ask about "response chunking/aggregation behavior" for SSE paths; 2) as a workaround, increase ALB idle timeout to 180s (if acceptable) and have origin send keepalives every 10s rather than 15s; 3) try toggling "Origin Keep-alive Timeout" in CloudFront if available.

Jen (support): I'll collect diag info from customer: distribution id, request id (X-Amz-Cf-Id), client tcpdump (if they can), and a short curl session showing timeline. Maria — can you ask them to run this quick trace and paste results?

curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://.../stream" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'

and also capture the header lines that show via/x-cache and the request id.

Maria G: On it. Also adding: we observed one case where CloudFront returned a 502 when ALB half-closed while CloudFront still expected a response. Might be related to the ALB timeout hitting during a small pause.

Tom (eng): That 502 fits ALB closing connection mid-stream. If customer can't change CloudFront quickly, recommend increasing ALB idle timeout and/or making server send an extra whitespace line every 9s to keep origin-to-edge TL alive.

sre-bot: Incident note created: SST-5235 "Customer SSE disconnects via CloudFront/ALB" — assigned to Kevin L. Please attach logs and CloudFront trace.

Jen (support): Thanks all. I'll follow up when I have the curl output + CF IDs. If we confirm CloudFront rebuffering we'll escalate to their support and run a canary without CF.

Maria G: Thanks — will update thread with outputs shortly. :thumbsup:
